title: SQL Injection - Authentication Bypass via Login Form
impact: An attacker can bypass authentication entirely and log in as any user including the administrator without knowing the password by manipulating the SQL query's logic through unsanitized input in the email field
remediation: Use parametized queries/prepared statements instead of concatenating user input directly into SQL strings so injected SQL syntax cannot alter the query's logic

title: SQL Injection — Data Extraction via Product Search (UNION-based)
column16: An unauthenticated attacker can extract arbitrary data from any table in the database — including user emails and password hashes — through the public product search endpoint by closing out the intended query and appending a UNION SELECT against the Users table
column17: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for the search endpoint and apply least privilege to the database account so it cannot query tables outside its intended scope

title: Reflected XSS via Product Search Query
owasp: An attacker can craft a malicious link containing this payload in the search query and trick a victim into clicking it when the victim's browser loads the page injected JavaScript executes in their session which could be used to steal session tokens or perform actions on the victim's behalf
mitre_attack: Sanitize and/or HTML-encode user-supplied input before reflecting it back into the page and apply a Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict inline script and iframe execution
